text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Wine company Casa do Douro is to sign an agreement, proposed by the government, which is aimed at resolving its financial difficulties, company president Mesquita Montes told the paper.
- The organisers of Lisbon's Expo-98 world exhibition expect to have invested around 183 billion escudos between 1994 and 1999.
- Retailer Jeronimo Martins is to enter the Hungarian market, said group president Soares dos Santos.
- Around 100 million families who borrowed from banks to buy houses in the 1980s are now struggling to pay back increasing debts.
- In 1997 Portuguese cereal producers will receive fewer funds from the EU as a penalty for excess production in 1996. EU cuts may be round 21 percent.
- Forty people stole 1.5 billion escudos from banks with false cheques and lost it all in casinos. It is one of the biggest frauds in Portugal in recent years.
- The spiralling cost of Lisbon's Expo-98 world exhibition is worrying the government.

- The final round of salary negotiations between the government and public sector trade unions take place today. The UGT, which has links to the ruling Socialist Party, seems willing to accept 3 percent, but Portugal's largest union, the communist CGTP, wants a 4.5 percent increase.
- French car company Renault may lay off 181 workers in its company in the Cabo Ruivo area of Lisbon. Trade unions have called for a strike on December 19.
